summary.one_liner: Clippinator (formerly Clippy) is a GPT-4 based autonomous code assistant that plans, writes, debugs, and tests software projects with a human giving feedback.
summary.what_it_does: Runs a set of cooperating GPT-4 agents on a project directory, coordinated by a main agent called Taskmaster that asks the user some questions, has an Architect plan the project structure, and then delegates writing, debugging, and testing to subagents (Architect, Writer, Frontender, Editor, QA, Devops). The agents have tools for reading and writing files, running bash and Python, managing background processes, linting with pylint, browser automation with Selenium, and simple HTTP page fetching. Project structure is gathered with ctags and given to all agents along with linter output and a shared memory. The user can stop with ^C, which saves state so the run resumes later, and can give feedback to the main agent or edit the architecture manually. An optional SerpAPI key enables search.
use_cases: autonomously generating a small software project from a high-level description
AI-assisted coding with human feedback loops
planning and scaffolding a project architecture
automated writing and testing of web services
experimenting with multi-agent GPT-4 coding workflows
how_to_run: Add OPENAI_API_KEY (and optionally SERPAPI_API_KEY) to a .env file.
Install ctags, and pylint plus pylint-venv for linting.
notable: Multi-agent design with Taskmaster delegating to specialized minions like Architect, Writer, and QA
Architecture is plain text written by the Architect and shared with all agents
Stop with ^C and resume from the last saved state; ^C also injects feedback to the main agent
Linter output is fed back to agents after every file write
Shared memory tool lets agents persist notes across the run
caveats: Runs GPT-4 for long periods, so it is expensive in OpenAI API usage
Not perfect and makes mistakes; the README says it works best with human supervision on harder tasks
Requires several external tools to be installed (Poetry, ctags, pylint, pylint-venv)
